Drop redundant external models from a panel

dedupExternals.Rd

Removes external models that duplicate one already kept, keeping the first occurrence of each near-identical set. Called automatically by BRIERi, BRIERi.cv, BRIERs, BRIERi.bopt and BRIERs.bopt whenever more than one external model is supplied, and exported so the same reduction can be inspected or applied on its own.

Usage

dedupExternals(
  beta.external,
  cor.min = 0.9,
  intercept.row = FALSE,
  labels = NULL
)

Arguments

beta.external

A numeric matrix of external coefficients, p x M for the summary-level convention or (p+1) x M with a leading intercept row for the individual-level one.

cor.min

Similarity threshold in (0, 1]. A model is dropped when its absolute cosine similarity with an already-kept model reaches this value. NULL or NA disables de-duplication entirely.

intercept.row

Logical. TRUE when the first row of beta.external is an intercept rather than a predictor coefficient, as BRIERi requires. The intercept is held out of the similarity computation and carried along with its column.

labels

Optional character vector of length M naming the external models, used in the report. Defaults to the column names, then to positional labels.

Value

A list with elements:

beta.external

The panel with redundant columns removed.

keep

Integer indices of the surviving columns in the input.

dropped

A data.frame of the removed columns with the reason for each, or NULL when nothing was removed.

M.in, M.out

Column counts before and after.

cor.min

The threshold used.

applied

Logical, whether any column was removed.

note

Character report lines, empty when nothing was removed.

Details

Two kinds of redundancy are removed. First, any model whose absolute cosine similarity with an already-kept model reaches cor.min. Second, any model that the kept set spans exactly, which pairwise similarity cannot see: a model equal to the sum of two others is uncorrelated with either. Columns that are entirely zero are also dropped, since they transfer nothing and put a zero on the diagonal of the stacking Gram matrix.

The test is on the coefficient vectors, not on the polygenic scores they produce. If one coefficient vector is a multiple of another then their scores agree in every metric, whatever the linkage disequilibrium is, so a drop here is provable from the coefficients alone and needs no LD matrix. The converse does not hold: two weakly correlated coefficient vectors can still give collinear scores through LD. The rule is deliberately conservative in that direction, and leaves LD-induced collinearity to the fitter.

Similarity is the uncentred correlation. Centring would be wrong here: these vectors are mostly zeros by construction, since a predictor an external model does not cover enters as a zero coefficient, and the quantity stacking inverts is an uncentred inner product.

See also

reduceExternalsPCA, calcExtY, calcExtXtY

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
b1 <- c(rep(1, 5), rep(0, 45))
beta.external <- cbind(b1, b1 * 2, rnorm(50))
ded <- dedupExternals(beta.external, cor.min = 0.9)
ded$keep
ded$dropped
} # }
